Our goal is to find total possibilities as sum(S!).

At first glance, there appears to be double-counting here, but actually it follows naturally from how Python handles duplicates during concatenation.

With more than one letter, duplicate pairs such as (‘aab’, ‘abb’) come together and share factors leading towards a balanced distribution throughout our final product.
So instead of adding twice, we divide each calculated factor by 2!
